text:
aj: Heads up — seeing a consistent 12-18% perf regression on the paged+fused Flash variant when the scheduler hands off batches from 32 -> 64. Only reproducible on interleaved KV layout with bf16 and odd stride alignments. seq=1024, model=redwood-small. :thinking:
perf-bot: perf-check: run=job-8417, model=redwood-small, seq=1024, batch=64, p95_latency=420ms (+17%), token_throughput=86k (-14%)
maria: Do we have profiler traces? bank-conflict symptoms — lots of stalled warps in shared mem. Any memcpy/pack logs around the handoff?
kevin: I captured a quick nvprof snippet on canary host (trimmed):
```
$ nvprof --section-memory ./run_bench
GPU activities:  stalled_cycles=1.2e9, achieved_occupancy=0.48
Mem throughput: 9.8 GB/s (expected 120 GB/s)
Kernel flash_hybrid_int8: shared_mem_bank_conflicts=23
Kernel fused_paged_bf16: shared_mem_bank_conflicts=3
```
sophia: That looks like the kernel selection changed to flash_hybrid_int8 path which assumes contiguous per-kv pages, but our packer produced interleaved banking to spread hotspots. Kernel expects bank-aligned stride; interleaving breaks that and causes conflicts.
aj: So root cause hypothesis = scheduling/batching handshake doesn't communicate layout/dtype/stride expectations to kernel selector. When batch grows in-flight we don't re-evaluate layout_hint and end up running incompatible kernel.
maria: Agreed. Two quick mitigations: 1) conservative kernel choice for unknown layout (pick fused/paged which does explicit align-copies), 2) cheap runtime align-check before dispatch and do a single memcpy to aligned temp if mismatch. Both would avoid the conflict at cost of a little memcpy.
kevin: Proposed proto change: include layout_hint in the scheduling token: `{dtype,bank_count,bank_stride,page_size,layout_type}`. Kernel selector uses it to prefer kernels and to toggle fast-path vs copy-path. Small change in router/pool handshake.
sophia: Also update batching heuristics: when batch crosses page boundary (e.g., total_kv_bytes / page_size changes), re-evaluate layout_hint and possibly re-pack current batch. Right now we bake layout at first request in batch.
aj: Plan: 1) add layout_hint to scheduler token, 2) kernel selector consults runtime align test, 3) packer exposes an align-copy helper, 4) benchmarks across dims. Kevin can PR.
kevin: I'll run microbenches matrix: layouts={interleaved,separate}, dtype={bf16,int8}, batch={1,8,32,64}, seq={512,1024}. Will instrument bank-conflict counters and wall-clock. Start now, full run by EOD.
perf-bot: bench-queue: job-8421 queued (params: kevin-matrix-2026-03-17)
sophia: Also add a lightweight fast-path in kernel selector: if (stride % 16 != 0 || bank_count % 4 != 0) prefer fused_paged_copy_kernel. That rules out pathological bank misalignment cheaply.
maria: +1. Once kevin posts numbers let's pick which route to take for canary (copy-mitigate vs conservative kernel). If copy is cheap it's better overall.
infra-bot: deploy-canary: kernel-selector v2 rolled to 4 canary hosts (hosts: canary-3..6). Watch the perf dashboard.
kevin: Quick update from canary run: fused kernels recovered throughput, flash_hybrid still sees ~6% drop vs baseline, but bank-conflict counters reduced after enabling align-copy. Suggests memcpy path mitigates, but there's still some extra branching in flash path.
aj: Sounds like a plan: land layout_hint + align-copy, add batch re-eval on page boundary, and then run full fleet canary. Thanks team — please paste benchmark links here when available. :thumbsup:
